page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an ARM64-based Microsoft Azure Cobalt/Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 32 physical cores with one thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache pool. System memory is configured at 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight notable strengths in memory throughput and multi-threaded throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 436.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.19 GB/sec, corresponding to a top-tier PassMark memory score and top-tier PassMark database operations. Compute evaluations reflect strong multi-core scaling, evidenced by high throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench compilation tests, and stress-ng multi-core suites, despite average single-thread baseline marks.

Without integrated local NVMe storage, disk throughput relies entirely on remote networked volumes. The single-threaded-to-multi-threaded performance distribution indicates that the platform delivers high cost efficiency for memory-intensive parallel workloads. It is well matched for enterprise in-memory caching, distributed relational or document databases, large-scale software compilation pipelines, and transactional backend architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz and 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The hardware architecture incorporates a 128 MB L3 cache and supports hardware AES encryption, though it provides no bundled local disks or GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles demonstrate top-tier memory bandwidth across uncached read and write operations, alongside high multi-threaded throughput in database operations, software compilation, and compression routines. Single-core performance remains average. Relying on remote storage attachments, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for horizontally scaling memory-bound workloads, rendering it suitable for distributed databases, caching clusters, and enterprise analytics services.
